steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: I'm back.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Lisburn, what are you standing around for?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Oh yeah, I remember now. Old Turiels' daughter was cooking in the back kitchen, so you wanted some excuse to slip on over.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Look at you, acting like you're doing us a great service.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: She used to work as a chef in a nearby restaurant, so it makes plenty of sense to bring her onboard.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Whatever. More importantly, why's the food not ready yet?

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Hey boss, how come the food hasn't been served yet?

steps.name: Server
steps.text: Sorry about that.

steps.name: Server
steps.text: The main reason is that we're a bit overloaded right now. Even though we've upped the kitchen staff, it's still not enough to handle the workload.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: In that case, l don't mind lending a hand!

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: There's no need.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Who are you...?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I am chief maid to the Saintess, Kjarr. It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Hah, we're just a bunch of lowly soldiers. No need for the formalities.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Lia.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Yes, Madam?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Split the accompanying servants into teams and have them take turns helping in the kitchen.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Make sure the banquet proceeds smoothly.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: But... we couldn't possibly have you–

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: There's no need to worry, sir.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Though this banquet is hosted by the Lord Viscount, this land is still Kjerag, and you are all esteemed guests in the eyes of the Saintess.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: As the Lord Viscount was gracious enough to extend an invitation to the Saintess, it is only natural that we servants lend our assistance as well.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Additionally... Pardon me if this may sound offensive, but it would be out of place for those whose hands wield weapons to carry plates.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Ngh...

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Calm down, Lisburn. The maid's right. We'd probably end up breaking a whole bunch of crockery if we tried to help.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: But, if there's any physical labor that needs doing, you just give us a holler, alright?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Oh, come to think of it, the kitchen could use some extra hands to help them carry some groceries. I'm not sure if...

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: I'm on my way!

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Thanks, Madam.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: My pleasure.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Now that things are settled here, I won't further disturb your enjoyment of the banquet.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: ...I'm back.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Lia, I have one more favor to ask of you. Can you see if the kitchen has these items? If they do, I'd like them to make one additional dish.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I'd like... a fruit and cheese wrap.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Pulling out the old home cooking?

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: But the Saintess normally doesn't touch that stuff.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Now, now. Just listen to me.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Karlan Trade's employees seem to be arriving one after another.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: That's right. The viscount invited not only the Saintess and Master Enciodes, but also the elders of the Vine-Bead Court as well as the employees of Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: As extravagant as one would expect of a Victorian viscount.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: The man's not all show either. He even invited Turiels, head chef of the Burdenpeak Hotel.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: His foul temper isn't something that can be bought with money.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: It goes to show how well they've gotten on with our people during the month they've been in Kjerag.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Chug! Chug!

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: *hic*... Chug, chug!

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: *braaaaap*...

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Not bad, not bad! You mountain folk sure know how to hold your booze!

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: But you still can't out-drink me! Heh... hehe.

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Who's up next?

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Urgh. Those men can get sloshed, even in a place like this?

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Not to mention, quite a few have already ended up under the table.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Kjarr, what should we do?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Getting on well is certainly a wonderful thing, but getting on too well can be problematic.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: This sort of thing, however, ends up being a headache for certain other people.

steps.name: Valais
steps.text: Gnosis, the Tschäggättä are in position.

steps.name: Valais
steps.text: I have them patrolling the front and rear entrances to prevent anyone from sneaking inside the venue.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: No need to be nervous.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Valais, send one team to go help in the kitchen.

steps.name: Valais
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Care for a drink? If you dare, that is.

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Th-This is some crazy strong stuff. We seriously doing this?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: As I said, up to you.

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Haha, you got me. You've got guts, I'll give you that. Cheers!

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Pour me another glass.

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: On it!

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: You're... not bad...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Do we have a hangover remedy?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Lia.

steps.name: Servant
steps.text: Right here.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: Huh? D-Director?!

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Enjoy your nap?

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: Uh, y-yes!

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: That one soldier with a stomach of iron... You managed to drink him under the table?!

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: That's crazy...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Lay off the alcohol for the rest of the day. Go rest.

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: Th-Thank you very much.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Color me surprised. I didn't expect Karlan Trade's CTO to be such a good drinker.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I can hardly tell from your face that you just downed two bottles of strong liquor.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Just some useless tricks I picked up when I was younger.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Did you frequently attend such occasions in your youth?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: The banquet will start soon, and I'll have Karlan Trade's employees help move things along.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You're not going to join in the conversation, Master Gnosis?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Not at the moment.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: It's their time now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Umm, you two––

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Why are you so taciturn today, Sir Enciodes? Is there something on your mind, or has coming to the banquet soured your mood?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Your usual quips and retorts are nowhere to be heard today.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I appreciate the Saintess's concern.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But, it's simply that sitting at the same table as the Saintess is a terrifying affair, and I can only hold my tongue in her presence.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I see. I did not think Sir Enciodes the pious type, but I stand corrected.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I dare not speak out of line.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Oh? There are things in this world that even Sir Enciodes dares not do?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Um... Haha, look how nice the weather is today. Perfect day to be holding a banquet, wouldn't you say?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Why don't you two go–

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Given the Saintess's high praise, there are naturally many things I am afraid of.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I won't prattle on with the details, but take the ceremony for Kjeragandr's statue the day after tomorrow. For such an important occasion, all of Karlan Trade must come together as one, without a single misstep.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: That being the case, I would recommend you be thorough and circumspect as well, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The completion of Kjeragandr's statue is of utmost importance to Kjerag. Not to mention, we are in the presence of our Victorian guests who are eager to 'congratulate' us. There is no such thing as too much caution.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It is as you say.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The Saintess is well-versed in all things divine, and the multitude of preparations made for the ceremony are impeccable and well thought-out. In all respects, a true blessing upon Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: As for all other affairs, please rest assured that Karlan Trade will take care of the Vine-Bead Court's concerns.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now, then. It's certainly reassuring to see the two of you so young and promising!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: As a reminder, we're not only here to celebrate, but also to discuss a collaboration––

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Seeing as how you're eloquent as ever, you seem to have no shortage of confidence.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You've been quite busy making a name for yourself, Sir Enciodes. Though I rarely go down the mountain, news of Karlan Trade's exploits are regularly reaching my ears.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But, please do not forget this, Sir Enciodes. For thousands of years, Kjerag has relied on hard work and pragmatism from generation to generation to develop our homeland into what it is today, not utilitarianism and reckless adventurism.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The Silverashes will never forget Kjeragandr's admonition of Her people.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: However, the Saintess must also understand that along with the people of Kjerag's hard work and pragmatism is an indomitable adventuring spirit, and a desire to ascend the highest summits.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Perhaps a little bit of this spirit is also what we need when it comes to dealing with external developments.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I only hope that your enthusiasm does not lead you headfirst into danger.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, the young truly are so full of energy. But, the Saintess is correct. Sometimes, stability is, in fact, necessary.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I invited the two of you here because I wanted to––

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I am truly touched by the Saintess's concern.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Please rest assured that I will handle this matter, and not betray your expectations.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: All things in Kjerag must inevitably answer to Kjeragandr's will.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Without sufficient faith, is it not true that I would struggle to take even a single step?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...You're just as awful as you ever were!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Ditto.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Gah, you two! If you have a disagreement, talk it through like adults! Don't go and ruin the peace!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Let's move on and discuss our cooperation––

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Sir Enciodes, your brain is as hard and stubborn as the purest Originium ice crystal.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The Saintess remains unmoving and... speaks bluntly for the first time in a long while.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I can't hold a candle to you in that regard.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But it seems that even after all these years, our great Sir Enciodes still has not learned to retain his capital.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: To what does the Great Saintess refer?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Have your old habits not flared up again? Taking on every bit of risk with no regard for the consequences?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The greater the risk, the greater the reward.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I hope you won't regret your choices later on down the road.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Nobody's going to sneak money under your pillow today!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Indeed, that won't be happening again.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: No longer will I be woken by the jingling of coins, or have to buy candies and snacks on margin and pay back thrice the amount.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I never asked you to pay me back!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Please, you two––

steps.name: Enciodes & Enya
steps.text: Just one moment please, Your Lordship.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh*... Fine, I suppose I'll drink to myself for now...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Holy Saintess, Sir Enciodes, I have no intention of involving myself in your private affairs.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But, if the Saintess has her own thoughts about Kjerag's present situation...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Then, reciprocating the Duke's offer may be the perfect option for you.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Holy Saintess, might I tell you what I've found most impressive about Kjerag?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Please do.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I recall the time I paid a medical call to a herdsman, Leones was his name. A young beast in his herd had gotten lost while grazing.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I offered to help him search for it, but he declined and told me not to worry.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: He had me wait until sundown, and left to have supper.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And so I waited.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: After finishing the treatment, I set up a cooking pot over the grass with him. We lit the pot, and he found a good piece of cheese. You should've heard the sizzling sound it made when he threw it in.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I was sitting to the side on a short bench, still thinking about the young beast, when I heard a high-pitched cry in the distance.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This might be something you see all the time in Kjerag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But for me, when I saw that young beast returning to the pasture at sunset; the way it found its way back to its mothers side, the two nuzzling against each other––

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What I felt at that moment... was something I don't know how to describe.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Old Leones told me that burdenbeasts recognize the scent of their kin, especially foals, which are particularly sensitive to their mother's scent.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Even if they get lost, they'll always find their way back by following their mother's scent.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: That blood bond reminds me of the way the people of Kjerag view their land.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It reminds me... of the way Sir Enciodes gave up Victoria in all her glory to return to Kjerag.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I see Your Lordship speaks very highly of Sir Enciodes. It is true that he has made many achievements thus far––

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But if you are comparing him to a young burdenbeast returning to his homeland thanks to his ties with his 'mother' by the name of Kjerag, I find that joke quite droll.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It is indeed thanks to Sir Enciodes's longing for his homeland that House Caster decided to fund Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Moreover, the Duke believed that since Sir Enciodes greatly treasured the Kjerag blood flowing in his veins, he likewise would not come to despise the other half of his blood–

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The Caster bloodline.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Holy Saintess, as I have previously stated, I am not here to stoke conflict.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But, at the inception of Karlan Trade, it was Caster who extended a helping hand to Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And now that Sir Enciodes has proven his worth, the Duke believes that it is time to collect a bit of interest.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It appears that a few pieces of candy will no longer be sufficient, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's not so complicated, really. What the Duke wants is simply a show of sincerity.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Her Grace wishes to see this goodwill from Sir Enciodes, from Karlan Trade, and ultimately, from Kjerag itself.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A show of sincerity towards the Duke of Caster, and towards Victoria.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So long as this sincerity exists, then our future cooperation will only become more intimate.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And if we fail to express such sincerity?
Harold puts down his tableware, then walks over to the window and opens it.
The cold wind laced with snow and ice instantly pours into the room. Even the burning stove is helpless to resist the chill.
He quickly closes the window once more.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, my apologies.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The Saintess's question was so incisive, I found myself wanting a breath of fresh air.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: After staying in this warm room for so long, I had forgotten how cold it was outside, you see.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: That being the case, Your Lordship could have simply entertained Sir Enciodes at this banquet. Why is my presence necessary?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well, you see, I've been eating and drinking remarkably well here. During my morning constitutional, my blood pressure had gone down even as my blood sugar was up a tad.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I wouldn't mind staying here for another year or so.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But you see, I find the Duke's incessant nagging quite bothersome.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Nowadays, Karlan Trade has become a pillar of Kjerag, and the kinship between the Great Saintess and Sir Enciodes runs deep.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I simply wanted to provide an opportunity for the two of you to sit down and talk things over.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I would like you to help me convince Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I appreciate Your Lordship's candor.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: However, everything that has a beginning must also have an end.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It is true that Kjerag owes much of its current standing to Karlan Trade; but if I, as the Saintess, were to say that I know nothing of this, it would simply be avoiding responsibility.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If you accept that I am the leader of this nation, then it must follow that I am also responsible for its current condition.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I cannot come up here and confidently proclaim that the ways of the past were wrong.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Sir Enciodes always boasts about how he was the one who chose Kjerag's current path.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: However, to this day, everything in Kjerag is the result of decisions that we have collectively made as a people, of which I am but one member.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Sir Enciodes himself has no right to rebuke Kjerag, as she is today.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And the same is true for me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...I see now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It seems I really ought to try more of Kjerag's food while I still have the appetite.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Please come with me, both of you.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Once again, I must thank you for your hospitality today, My Lord.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I hope my choice of dishes will suit both your tastes. They are traditional Kjerag dishes that I specially requested Chef Turiels prepare.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Wow, this cheese wrap looks positively splendid!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Cheese wraps? And, there are even fruit chunks inside...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: ...Truly, a traditional household dish.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Dig in, my friends. Don't be shy.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: After you, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Very well... if you insist.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: ...That smell again.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You still remember it?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis should be here. Where is he?

steps.name: Karlan Trade Employee
steps.text: Sir, there were these Victorian soldiers earlier...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Soldiers?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It all makes sense now.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It would be unbefitting of the Saintess to personally appear before Victorian soldiers, no?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Do as you will. Don't worry about me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now then, I shall not take up any more of your time, Holy Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It really is that same smell.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh*—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: At least the bit of silver lining is the Trilby Ashers can't accuse me of doing nothing.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I've done what needed doing, and the ceremony is about to begin. I suppose it's time to head back.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh right, can't forget to pick up souvenirs for the wife and daughter.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And also––

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Alas, it would be remiss of me to leave any regrets behind on this trip.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, there you are, Madam Degenbrecher.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I see you've found yourself a lovely spot! Clean and––

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hey now, don't go!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you want an audience, go talk to Enciodes. Or Gnosis.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'll have nothing to do with your little games.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Come now. That's no way to be talking.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: With all this delicious food and drink in front of you, would it really kill you to exchange a few pleasantries?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: For example, shall we toast?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Nein danke.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh? Are you a woman who can't handle her drink?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'm much better at handling men who try to ply me with drink.

spans.text: men who try to ply me with drink.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Shall I prove it to you?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hahaha! No need, I'll take your word for it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, right. Lily's in fine shape now, thanks to your timely handling of the matter.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I've already arranged for follow-up care, and her little ones are in good health as well.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Leones said to leave one for you to name.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: ...I'm glad things worked out.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And I'll pass on that last part. Don't have much of a naming sense.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Aha! In that case, why not let me do it for you?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Never fear. Naming is a bit of a science in Victoria, and I happen to have a bit of expertise in the field!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The little one is a girl, so my suggestion would be to name her Olivia Turnbottom Michelle Craigavon!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I put together my last name, my wife's maiden name, and my grandmother's first name, making her the same as my daughter's––

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I've changed my mind. Her name's Dolor.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*––!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: B-But I wasn't finished yet, Madam Degenbrecher––

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Her name is Dolor.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But, Olivia...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Dolor.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ..Alright, alright!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Dolor, umm, is also a fine name for a girl. 'Healthy and strong', right?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Even though I still think Olivia Turnbottom Michelle Craigavon has a bit more charm to it...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Nevertheless, I think Leones will be quite fond of the name, fitting as it is for a Kjerag girl.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher, I also have another favor to ask of you, presumptuous as it may be. Please take a look at this... I'm afraid I'll be leaving empty handed on this business trip.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I would at least like to leave a little memento for myself, as a personal note.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: As I said back at the station, I'm a huge fan of yours, see? Would you be willing to give me your autograph?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You don't seem like the type to obsess over knightsports.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You think too highly of me. Vulgar man that I am, far be it from me to avoid vulgar pleasures.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Though the arena is certainly different from the battlefield, the victors all have something that elevates them above the crowd.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It certainly is a fine pastime–– and I hope you take no offense to me saying that, as none is intended.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: That much is true.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You say that, but you still refuse to give this poor old man your autograph, even as he's holding this card out.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I've treasured this trading card for a long time, you know. It was a limited release from the first time you won the Major. You never released another card...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's a darn shame that I can't seem to win your favor no matter what.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: That aside, when it comes to naming, there is something I've been curious about, and would appreciate if you could shed some light on the matter. Of course, you don't have to answer if you find it offensive.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: 'Degenbrecher' –– Is that your real name?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're certainly brave to ask, Craigavon.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm a man of few talents, but courage is something I do carry.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What if it is?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Just consider it scratching the itchy curiosity of your fans, Madam.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: After all, every angle of your being has been under the spotlight since the first time you won the Major. The origins of the Black Knight, and where her path ultimately led her... Countless eyes have been following you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Which brings me to my next question, Madam Degenbrecher, is your contract with Karlan Trade about to expire?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I do wonder if you'd spare me the honor of inviting you to be a guest of Victoria? No doubt, the Duke would be more than glad to welcome your arrival, and perhaps, we'd even be able to discuss new horizons of cooperation...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Uh huh. Is that all you wanted to ask?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If that's all you're here for, I've heard you out. Now, if you'd leave me in peace––

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I've spent a decade in Kjerag.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'm one of her people.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And I plan to live out my days here.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Good enough for you?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah... Yes, that's exactly what I wanted to hear.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I had my own speculation about the answer, but I must admit, it was quite moving to hear it in your own words... Why, you didn't even try to dress it up with more local flair!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: True, I suppose you're dressed with a bit of color.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Where'd you get the fur collar?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, this is from a souvenir shop I'm rather partial to. It's quite warm.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Alright, alright. It's getting late and the banquet should be drawing to an end soon, so I won't pester you any longer.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Though I wasn't fortunate enough to win your signature, I do want to say one thing...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I enjoyed our chat very much, Madam.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Please watch your step, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Chester
steps.text: Enciodes, I've brought the car.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Thank you, Uncle.

steps.name: Chester
steps.text: Are you returning to the mansion?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Back... to the office...

steps.name: Chester
steps.text: Enciodes?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What he said. There are still some chores I need to take care of.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Long time no see, Uncle Chester.

steps.name: Chester
steps.text: Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Just call me by name on these occasions.

steps.name: Chester
steps.text: Enya... I'm so glad to see you safe and sound.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The feeling is mutual. I'm relieved that you're in good health.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now then, I shall take my leave, Holy Saintess, Sir Enciodes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: My Lord.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Yes, Holy Saintess?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: All else aside, I hope you have a wonderful time in Kjerag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...Thank you for your kind words.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Yes, Saintess?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Please have the maids clean the mess.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Oh, there's no need for that.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: The good soldiers not only helped clean everything up, but even took away the leftover food. They said they were going to bring it to the Infected soldiers who weren't able to attend the banquet.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: This Viscount actually seems quite respectable. It feels as if he's playing the villain.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Though, I trust that's something Sir Enciodes here can relate to.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You flatter me, Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It's getting dark. Be careful on your way back.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You too.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Did you need something else?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In the name of Kjeragandr, Kjerag has arrived where she is today despite the gulf between us.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What would Kjeragandr think, were She to look down upon Her land today? Would She condemn us?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Are you getting cold feet?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Of course not. The miracle three years ago will forever be engraved in the hearts of all Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Even I must admit that Kjeragandr indeed is the bedrock of this land.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We are all but children playing atop Her body.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If so, that question isn't for me to answer.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Perhaps, it's not for Her to answer either.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Alright, we're back.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I can go the rest of the way myself.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Oh, really?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: ...It was just a minor miscalculation.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Hold on, I need a moment.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Certainly.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: No, not at the main door. Head around the side.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What's the problem? Worried someone might see you?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Someone might be working overtime.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Who'd be working overtime at this hour?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Me.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: And you too, probably.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Are you complaining that I haven't given you enough overtime pay?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Alright, Gnosis, sit down already. Nobody will see the drunken and indecent behavior of the CTO.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If you ask me, you're holding your own image to too high a standard.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: You're a lot more talkative after a few drinks, Enciodes.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: If anything, you owe Degenbrecher more overtime pay.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: He actually owes me a few lives.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Too lazy to keep count.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The two leaders of Karlan Trade, squatting in the lobby of the company headquarters in the middle of the night to discuss unpaid wages?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis is fighting on your behalf.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Did the booze melt his brain?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: It's not like I got sloshed for your sake––
Degenbrecher looks over at Enciodes, who only gives a shrug.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What an embarrassment.
Degenbrecher hands the canteen of water she brought over to Enciodes, and the latter naturally reaches out to accept it.
The last decade has seen countless such moments.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Do you still remember Walden's?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The first time you had to carry me and Gnosis back.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Oh, that banquet.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Where Gnosis got piss drunk and you didn't, yet you were worse for wear because of it.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Look at him now. His liver is clearly a lot tougher these days.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: At least he's not passing out all over the place.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You sure this one's still conscious?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Before you two start badmouthing me to my face, blurgh––

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Can you bring me some hangover remedy?
The man slumped over on the steps does not lift his head, merely stretching his hand out towards his ill-spirited friend.
Degenbrecher raises her eyebrows, then takes a pack of pills out of her pocket and places them in Gnosis's hand.
She watches him open up the blister pack with practiced motions and swallow the contents along with a big gulp of water. After a while, she lets out a sigh of relief.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: That's a bit better.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: But this doesn't seem to be the same medicine I took before.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's not a hangover cure.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's a poison I made.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Enciodes put me up to it.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Yes, quite right.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Is that so? Then, why am I not dead yet? Doesn't seem like your poison's very effective.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: How dull... Are you two not tired of this routine yet?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I thought it was pretty funny.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It was more fun back when you actually believed it and tried to make yourself vomit.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: That was years ago.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But, that was a different pill, wasn't it?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It didn't look the same as the previous one.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Riley sent it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: He often goes drinking with the Victorians and says this one works better.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Enciodes, it seems that Degenbrecher has become the most popular of us three among the people of Kjerag.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Noticed the promotional pictures of the Black Knight hanging off the burdenbeast billboards by the station?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Hand-drawn, too.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Is that a problem?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I've become increasingly busy in recent years and have neglected many things.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Once the situation calms a bit, Gnosis and I really need to start going out more often.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: That's for sure.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you don't show your face in public every once in a while, people will start to worry about your private life.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: One popular line of speculation is that you've thrown yourself into work as you've been heartbroken over certain things.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There are quite a few variations too. Want me to give you a rundown?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Hahahahahahagah–– *cough* *cough* *cough*–– * Bluuurgh––

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I pray you don't choke to death laughing and vomiting at the same time, Gnosis.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If you could laugh like that all the time, our employees wouldn't be so afraid of you.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: *cough* *cough*– Don't worry, before I croak, I'll make sure to puke all over your shoes.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: So, how did your discussion today go? Reach any agreements?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: When it comes to matters concerning Kjerag, there aren't actually that many differences between me and the Saintess.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What about between you and the girl named Enya?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: ...The only problems worth talking about are those that can be resolved.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If I had to do things over again, I'd make the same decision every time. And she'd still never feel good about it.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We all know that deep down.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Say what you will, but you'll never tell that to her face.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're not much different, Gnosis.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're two peas in a pod.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Never saying what needs to be said to the people who need to hear it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Also, you should be playing dead right about now.
The lights of the office still shine bright in the night. The heating in the main hall is shut off, and silence spreads freely through the room, along with the cold.
A moment later, the silence is broken by the sound of Gnosis retching.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Degenbrecher, I need another pill.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: My head hurts.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: ...And a couple for me too. I might be a bit tipsy.
Both men stretch out their hands towards Degenbrecher at the same time.
That unflappable attitude that someone there knows the truth makes Degenbrecher tingle with irritation for some reason.
There are still many questions that cannot be answered.
But at least here, right in this moment, there's no need to show off, no need for pretense.
Degenbrecher heeds her own will, and slaps each of the two hands in turn.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Gah...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Stand up. Go home already, if you're drunk.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Don't squat here.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's a lot of work to be done tomorrow.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Now, go.
